title: Wednesday deadline to comment on parking changes in Rochdale, Littleborough and Milnrow
excerpt: Residents have until Wednesday 28 October to comment on three proposed parking orders affecting Mere Street, Wardle Street and the Butterworth Hall area.
body:
Drivers and residents have until Wednesday 28 October 2026 to object to or comment on three proposed parking restriction changes across Rochdale borough. The council has published notices of intent for Mere Street in Rochdale, Wardle Street in Littleborough and the Butterworth Hall and Royds Street area in Milnrow. These are proposals, not restrictions already in force.

On Mere Street, near Drake Street in the Milkstone and Deeplish ward, the proposal would shorten existing no waiting at any time restrictions on both sides of the road from 22 metres to 15 metres from the junction. That would release a small additional length for parking. The council says the change follows the introduction of one way working and pavement build outs, and is intended to improve local parking provision without compromising visibility. The order reference is H60/1456.

On Wardle Street in Littleborough, the council proposes new no waiting at any time restrictions on the north side for 10 metres from Whitelees Road, and on the south side between Whitelees Road and Frederick Street. Its stated reasons include junction visibility, narrow carriageway width and reports of vehicles parking on both sides or on the footway. The reference is H60/1457.

In Milnrow, the Butterworth Hall area proposal would introduce no waiting at any time restrictions on the south side of Butterworth Hall for 59 metres from Royds Street, and on the east side of Royds Street for 24 metres from Butterworth Hall. The council cites double parking and difficulties for refuse and other larger vehicles using the roads. The reference is H60/1459. The notice's heading labels the amendment as 2027, while its objection deadline is explicitly 28 October 2026; readers should use the council's order reference when asking for clarification.

Comments or objections must reach the council by 28 October. Residents can email trafficorders@rochdale.gov.uk or write to Network Management, Floor 2, Number One Riverside, Smith Street, Rochdale OL16 1XU, stating the relevant reference and the reasons for their objection. The council also accepts comments in support while the objection period is open.

The full notices, maps and reasons are available through the council's Traffic Regulation Orders page: https://www.rochdale.gov.uk/roadworks-repairs-restrictions/proposed-permanent-restrictions-highways-traffic-regulation-orders .

Would these proposals make your street safer, or make parking more difficult? Share your experience in the comments. Do not assume a proposal is already enforceable until the council confirms the final order.
